source.title: Don't Retrain, Align: Adapting Autoregressive LMs to Diffusion LMs via Representation Alignment
source.authors: Fred Zhangzhi Peng; Alexis Fox; Anru R. Zhang; Alexander Tong

record.tranche_reason: The study uses representation alignment as a tool for AR-to-diffusion conversion and reports conversion performance. It does not test whether independently trained models naturally converge in representation geometry.
record.gate_note: The paper deliberately aligns a bidirectional diffusion student to a frozen, same-checkpoint autoregressive teacher. It reports downstream code-generation scores, not direct measurements of cross-model distance geometry or spontaneous convergence. The reported performance results are recorded as findings about the alignment method, under fits_no_version. The public-DLM comparison evaluates the full recipe and does not isolate representation alignment.
record.test_reason: The study deliberately aligns a bidirectional diffusion student to a frozen AR teacher from the same checkpoint, then reports only code-generation scores for its own method. It never measures representational similarity between independently trained models, so it bears on no version. Its claim that representations are 'universal regardless of generation order' is an interpretation, not a convergence measurement.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that cosine alignment to a frozen same-checkpoint AR teacher speeds AR→DLM conversion (up to 4×) and improves quality, with gains growing with size, and works on tiny data. They also assert that linguistic representations are 'universal regardless of generation order'. That assertion rests on downstream performance, not on any measurement of representational similarity.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a cosine hidden-state alignment loss during an intentionally trained AR-to-DLM conversion; it is not a replication of spontaneous cross-model convergence measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported downstream performance varies with alignment metric, alignment weight, and selected layer group. Cosine exceeds L2 on the reported HumanEval scores; λ = 20 performs below λ = 10; layer groups give different scores.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding layer-wise cosine alignment to a frozen same-checkpoint AR teacher raises HumanEval pass@10 over unaligned conversion: 24.9→31.0 at 0.6B and 31.1→40.5 at 1.7B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Anchoring an AR→DLM student to its AR teacher's hidden states improves conversion quality, with larger gains at larger size.

fits_no_version.finding: Downstream benefit depends on the alignment loss (cosine beats L2), its weight (peak at λ=10) and the layer group.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The benefit of representation-alignment training depends on its metric and settings.

fits_no_version.finding: With alignment and matched steps, a 0.8B-token subset gives higher HumanEval pass@1 and pass@10 than the full 50B stream.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Aligned AR→DLM conversion needs little data.

record.problems: The study is limited to same-architecture Qwen3 conversions and code-generation benchmarks. The paper reports point estimates without error bars, confidence intervals, or multi-seed significance tests. Its central alignment results concern downstream task performance, not direct quantitative measurements of representation geometry.
record.rows_left_out: No 60-row cap applied. Did not include the public-DLM frontier comparison, which evaluates the full recipe rather than isolating the alignment component. Did not add separate freezing or throughput rows because those results concern training efficiency and do not measure representation alignment or its effect against the unaligned baseline.

untested.parts: No measurement of alignment between independently trained models of different architectures, objectives or data, nor how it changes with scale. The size-dependent gain concerns downstream benefit from forced alignment, not spontaneous convergence.
No vision-language or paired cross-modal comparison.
No comparison across random seeds; the student is initialised from the teacher's weights.
No mapping, stitching or relative-representation test between independently trained models. The alignment is imposed by training, and no similarity score after training is reported.
No comparison of features, neurons or circuits across models.
The cosine-vs-L2 comparison is between training losses scored on HumanEval, not between similarity measures of convergence.
No measure of the degree of alignment, of plateaus, or of causes from shared data or objectives.

record.verdict_notes: Absolute pass@10 values for r1/r2 are in the Introduction (24.9→31.0 and 31.1→40.5). The 'universal representations' rhetoric touches the phenomenon but is untested in the sense the versions require: there are no independent models and no similarity scores. Single-seed point estimates only.

versions.untested_parts: No test of independently trained models with different architectures, objectives, or data naturally becoming more aligned with scale or capability.
No paired image-caption or other vision-language representation comparison.
No comparison across random initializations or analysis of shared features or subspaces.

The study directly optimizes hidden-state cosine alignment between a student and a teacher, but does not test whether an independently trained model can be mapped to another with little loss, or evaluate linear maps, stitching, relative representations, or unpaired mapping.
No comparison of recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits across models.
The cosine-versus-L2 ablation measures code-generation performance under alignment losses, not convergence under alternative similarity metrics, settings, or input distributions.
The study does not test whether alignment plateaus or whether shared data or objectives explain alignment.

relation.reason: Alignment is an imposed training objective; code-generation scores do not measure spontaneous convergence or interchangeability of independently learned representations.

tranche.reason: Uses deliberately trained representation alignment to a frozen teacher initialized from the same checkpoint and reports its conversion method's downstream performance; no claim version is tested.

source_check.notes: All listed rows report the study's own method performance and should be excluded as phenomenon evidence under the verdict rules; versions none and cannot_determine are appropriate. No listed statements or verdicts require checking.
